tip: Kvar means left or remaining. Stannar kvar means stays behind or lingers, adding the sense of not going away.
When som is the object of the clause you can drop it. Parken vi besöker means the same as Parken som vi besöker.
Swedish uses one word, som, for both who and that. Människor som pratar covers people who talk and things that do.
Past passive adds -s to the past tense. Bokade plus s gives bokades, meaning was booked, with no helper verb.
Det som means what, in the sense of the thing that. Det som gör covers what makes or what does something.
Den som means whoever or the one who. Den som frågar = whoever asks, used for general statements.
Vars means whose, the possessive relative word. Mannen vars hund = the man whose dog. It never changes form.
Blev plus a participle like öppnad builds a passive for one completed event, unlike the -s passive for general facts.
In a passive, av marks who does the action. Talas av tio miljoner = spoken by ten million.
Under with a time span means over or during. Under två år = over a period of two years, not underneath anything.
Inside a som clause the adverb comes before the verb. Jag aldrig har sett, not jag har aldrig sett as in a main clause.
Allt som allt is a set phrase meaning all in all or all things considered. It is not read literally.
Så vitt jag vet is a fixed phrase for as far as I know. Vitt here is not the color white.
Inte förrän means not until. Starting a sentence with it flips verb and subject, so it is fick vi, not vi fick.
Ha på sig is the idiom for wearing clothes. Hon har på sig = she has on, meaning she is wearing.
Träffas ends in -s to mean meet each other. The -s gives a mutual sense, so vi träffas = we meet up.
Brukade plus an infinitive means used to. Brukade besöka = used to visit, for a past habit that has stopped.
Varannan means every other. Varannan dag = every other day, alternating between on days and off days.
Adding -tiden to a clock hour means around that time. Vid åttatiden = around eight, not exactly eight.
For a place, use där (where) instead of som. Stugan där vi brukade bo = the cabin where we used to live.
Swedish uses på for days and holidays. På julafton = on Christmas Eve, just as på söndag = on Sunday.
